sources.snippet: The GGUF here is fully multimodal — text and vision. Most converted VL checkpoints in this collection ship a text-only GGUF, because the converter silently drops the vision tower. llama.cpp registers MiniCPM-V 4.7 properly, so the vision tower is shipped as a separate projector file, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B-heretic-mmproj-F16.gguf (1.11 GB), and the two files together are the model. sources.snippet: MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B-heretic will attempt offensive-security prompts that a hosted commercial model declines, which is what makes it usable for red-team corpus generation and for measuring what an unaligned model of this class produces.

sources.snippet: MiniCPM-V 4.7 is the latest model in the MiniCPM-V series, available in 35BA3B and 1B variants, with 35BA3B being the first MoE model in the MiniCPM-V series. It builds on the family's single-image, multi-image, and video understanding capabilities, combining stronger foundation capabilities with efficient visual encoding and on-device inference.
